newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat says metal strike has little response.
newsitem.headline: Fiat says metal strike has little response.

text.p: Italian carmaker Fiat said Friday's national strike by engineering and metalworkers had seen a fairly low turnout among its workforce.

Although trades unions termed the four-hour stoppage in support of a pay dispute a success, a Fiat spokesman said participation by its workers had been less than in the last strikes staged by the sector in November and September.
According to Fiat data, its main Turin Mirafiori plant saw 14.9 percent of the workforce striking in the body shop, 29.1 percent on assembly lines and 17.4 percent in the press shop.

At its southern Italian car factories, the Bravo/Brava plant at Cassino showed a strike level of 19.8 percent, the Alfa Romeo Pomigliano plant near Naples 7.7 percent, 33.6 percent at the Termini Imerese Punto plant in Sicily, and 20.03 percent at Melfi which makes the Punto and Lancia Y.
At trucks unit Iveco the strike level was 51 percent, at the MotoriAvio plant 44.7 percent and 65 percent at its Comau robotics plant.
But Giorgio Cremaschi, Piedmont regional secretary of the FIOM metalworkers' union, contested the figures.
"Even though companies continue to issue figures which don't correspond with reality as they did over the last strikes, today's strike has been a great success," he said.
Contracts for some 1.7 million metal and engineering workers expired in June but employers and unions have yet to reach an accord on new pay terms.
According to union figures, the strike level at the Mirafiori plant had been 80 percent in the press shop and assembly lines and some 60-70 percent in the body shop.
